summary: Switches between views of the same object without leaving the page: the tokens, components and reviews of one library. The selected tab is marked with the signal underline.
whenToUse: Two to seven peer views of the same context, where users switch back and forth.
underline for page and card sections; contained for a compact switch inside a toolbar (Light or Dark preview).
count to show how many items wait in a view, like open reviews.
Vertical orientation for settings pages with many sections next to their content.
whenNotToUse: Steps of a sequence the user must complete in order: use a stepper or a form with sections.
Navigation between pages with their own URL: use SidebarNav or links styled as tabs, not Tabs (which do not change the URL).
Changing a setting or filter value: use RadioGroup or an attached ButtonGroup.

dos.title: Short, parallel labels
dos.text: One or two nouns per tab, same grammatical form. The user scans them as a set.

donts.title: Tabs that are really actions
donts.text: "Export" or "Delete" in a tab list hides an action behind a view switch. Use a Button.

accessibility: Base UI Tabs: role tablist, tab and tabpanel, aria-selected, aria-controls and aria-labelledby are wired for you.
One tab stop for the whole list. Arrow keys move between tabs (Up and Down when vertical), Home and End jump, focus wraps by default.
By default arrows move focus and Enter or Space selects; set activateOnFocus when panels are cheap to render.
Give the TabsList an aria-label (or labelledby) so the tablist has a name.
The selected tab has a visible signal underline plus stronger text: never color alone.
Disabled tabs are announced as disabled and cannot be selected.
contentGuidelines: No verbs, no punctuation, no more than two or three words.
Counts are numbers in the count prop, not in the label text.

anatomy.label: Label
anatomy.indicator: Selection indicator (signal underline or raised plate)
